title: Year controls left three of four July warmth slopes uncertain for German elder flower-to-fruit intervals in 1961-2023
abstract: We tested July warmth and the time from elder flowering to the first ripe fruit in Germany. We used 111,507 paired station-years at 3,934 stations in 1961-2023. Four tests split North and South Germany and 1961-1990 and 1991-2023. Models had station means, May temperature, and either a trend or separate year means. Three of four July slopes had 95% intervals below zero with a trend. With year means, only South Germany in 1961-1990 had an interval below zero: -1.58 days per 1 C warmer July (95% interval -2.30 to -0.86). All four interval trend estimates included zero. Thus the data did not establish a common response across regions and periods. Long-record and next-year weather checks are reported. The model intervals group errors by station and year. Observer changes, selected paired records, coarse monthly weather, missing moisture and pollution measures, and shared regional weather limit interpretation. This test does not identify a causal effect of climate change. Code, source hashes, model summaries and a figure support reproduction. External source records and derived record tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: July temperature slopes and paired interval trends in four German samples. Bars show 95% two-way station/year cluster intervals. Most slopes become uncertain with year means.

citations.reason: Prior German timing work motivated station, year and period checks. We test paired elder flower-to-fruit intervals and do not reuse its record tables.
